quests.contextSentence: Ms. Ruan cancelled the workshop because it had too few sign-ups.
quests.ruleExplanation: The 'because' clause explains the cancellation. What had too few sign-ups is the workshop, not Ms. Ruan.
quests.nativeTip: 'Because' gives the reason. What had too few sign-ups?

quests.contextSentence: Mr. Dube complained to the manager because she had ignored his emails.
quests.ruleExplanation: The pronoun 'she' is feminine, so it cannot be Mr. Dube. The manager is the one who ignored the emails and caused the complaint.
quests.nativeTip: Who could have ignored the emails, and is 'she'?

quests.contextSentence: Because the app crashed twice, the developers said they would fix it before the weekend.
quests.ruleExplanation: The clause 'because the app crashed' sets up the problem. 'It' is what will be fixed, so it refers to the app.
quests.nativeTip: What crashed, and what needs fixing?

quests.contextSentence: Although Priya disliked the dentist's advice, she followed it.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Although' contrasts her dislike with her action. The thing she followed is the advice, not the person who gave it.
quests.nativeTip: What did she follow?

quests.contextSentence: Although the hotel was near the beach, it had no sea view.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Although' links two facts about the same subject. The hotel was near the beach, and the hotel had no view.
quests.nativeTip: What is being described in both clauses?

quests.contextSentence: Although the applicants had impressed the panel, it hired an external candidate.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'It' is singular, so the plural applicants are out. The panel makes the hiring decision after the contrast introduced by 'although'.
quests.nativeTip: 'It' is singular. Who does the hiring?

quests.contextSentence: When the alarm went off, the guard checked the doors while she called the police.
quests.ruleExplanation: Look closely: 'she' is singular and refers to the one who did both actions at once. That is the guard, the subject of the main clause.
quests.nativeTip: Who checked the doors, and is 'she'?

quests.contextSentence: While Jonas was cooking, his flatmate answered the door and told him the delivery had arrived.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Him' is the object of 'told'. The flatmate is the subject of that clause, so the person receiving the message is Jonas.
quests.nativeTip: Who is being told the news?

quests.contextSentence: When the referee blew the whistle, the players stopped and she pointed to the spot.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'She' is singular, so it is not the plural players. She is the referee, who blew the whistle and pointed.
quests.nativeTip: Who blew the whistle, and who is singular?

quests.contextSentence: After the technician replaced the fan, he tested it for an hour.
quests.ruleExplanation: Consider the form of 'it': it is the object of 'tested', so it points back to what was replaced: the fan. The technician is 'he'.
quests.nativeTip: What could be tested?

quests.contextSentence: Before the guests arrived, Mrs. Lim cleaned the flat and set the table for them.
quests.ruleExplanation: In this sentence, 'them' is plural and comes after the 'before' clause. The people she is preparing for are the guests.
quests.nativeTip: Who is the table set for?

quests.contextSentence: The inspector left after the workers told him the crane was unsafe, and they stopped work.
quests.ruleExplanation: Note that 'they' is plural. The workers are the group that reported the danger and stopped work, while the inspector is 'him'.
quests.nativeTip: Who told the inspector, and who stopped?

quests.contextSentence: If the patient feels dizzy, the nurse will take her to the ward.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Her' is an object pronoun. The nurse is the subject of 'take', so 'her' is the patient who feels dizzy.
quests.nativeTip: Who is being taken?

quests.contextSentence: Unless the bakery restocks its shelves by nine, customers will go elsewhere.
quests.ruleExplanation: Remember that 'its' is a singular non-human possessive. The bakery owns the shelves and will restock them.
quests.nativeTip: Which noun owns shelves?

quests.contextSentence: If the students hand in their projects late, the professor will deduct marks.
quests.ruleExplanation: Here, 'their' is plural and belongs to those who hand in. The projects are handed in by the students.
quests.nativeTip: Who hands things in?

quests.contextSentence: Since Deepa moved to Leeds, her parents have visited her every month.
quests.ruleExplanation: Here, 'her' is the object of 'visited'. The visitors are her parents, so the person visited is Deepa.
quests.nativeTip: Who is being visited?

quests.contextSentence: Since the company merged with its rival, staff have complained about the new system.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Its' refers to the subject of the 'since' clause, the company that merged. Staff are plural people.
quests.nativeTip: Whose rival is it?

quests.contextSentence: Since Karim's laptop stopped charging, he has borrowed his sister's, and she needs it back by Tuesday.
quests.ruleExplanation: In this sentence, 'she' is the sister, and she wants back what she lent, her laptop. Karim's own laptop is the one that stopped charging.
quests.nativeTip: Whose laptop would she want back?
quests.visualAnchor: 🔗 Pronoun 'it' points back to ➔ 'his sister's laptop'

quests.contextSentence: Rosa told her accountant that she had paid the tax bill, and he agreed that it was on time.
quests.ruleExplanation: Note that 'she' is feminine, so it cannot be the accountant, who is 'he'. The person who paid the bill is Rosa.
quests.nativeTip: Who paid the bill?

quests.contextSentence: Mr. Farah told the receptionist he had a nine o'clock appointment, and she asked him to wait.
quests.ruleExplanation: Look closely: 'he' is masculine, and the receptionist is 'she'. The person with the appointment is Mr. Farah.
quests.nativeTip: Whose appointment is it?

quests.contextSentence: The committee told the applicants that it had reached a decision, but they would have to wait until Wednesday.
quests.ruleExplanation: The pronoun 'it' is singular, so it cannot be the applicants. The committee reached a decision, and the applicants are the ones who wait.
quests.nativeTip: 'It' is singular. Who reached the decision?

quests.contextSentence: Nora handed the toddler the spoon while his mother held the bowl, and he immediately dropped it.
quests.ruleExplanation: Note that 'he' is masculine, so it cannot be his mother. The toddler was given the spoon and dropped it.
quests.nativeTip: Who is male and handling the spoon?

quests.contextSentence: When the plumber lifted the tiles, he found that they had been glued to the pipes.
quests.ruleExplanation: Remember that 'they' is plural. The tiles were lifted and found glued, while the pipes are what they were stuck to.
quests.nativeTip: What was glued to something?

quests.contextSentence: While the technician updated the software, the receptionist told the patients they could use the waiting room.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'They' is plural, so it cannot be the technician or the receptionist. The people who are told what they can do are the patients.
quests.nativeTip: Who is allowed to use the waiting room?

quests.contextSentence: Unless Ms. Ward approves the invoice, the accountant cannot pay it.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'It' is a thing that can be paid. Ms. Ward approves, and the accountant pays; the invoice is what they both handle.
quests.nativeTip: What can be paid?

quests.contextSentence: If Zara calls Mr. Ali before noon, he will send her the forms.
quests.ruleExplanation: Notice that 'he' is Mr. Ali, so 'her' must be someone else. The person who calls and gets the forms is Zara.
quests.nativeTip: Who will receive the forms?

quests.contextSentence: The team will keep its lead unless the rivals score twice.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Its' is singular, so it is not the plural rivals. The team currently has the lead and might lose it.
quests.nativeTip: Which group has the lead?

quests.contextSentence: Although the surgeon was tired, she reviewed the notes herself before the operation.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Herself' stresses that the surgeon personally reviewed the notes. It is feminine and singular, and it matches the subject.
quests.nativeTip: Who did the reviewing?

quests.contextSentence: After the customers complained about the queue, the supervisor opened another till and asked them to move over.
quests.ruleExplanation: Remember that 'them' is plural and is the object of 'asked'. The customers are the people in the queue who can move.
quests.nativeTip: Whom is she asking to move?

quests.contextSentence: Because the intern forgot to save her work, the supervisor asked her to redo it, and she agreed.
quests.ruleExplanation: Look closely: 'it' is the object of 'redo'. What she forgot to save and now has to redo is her work.
quests.nativeTip: What can be redone?
